title: Point-power normalized Roos comparison specialization
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D with algebraic closure k, a prime l and finite extension E of Q_l. Use the point-system inverse images F_r and G_r for recursively defined Frobenius powers and the exact scalar restriction U of [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Suppose P is a family of the compositors d_m,t_m and scalar restriction isomorphisms b_r of [def-trf-point-power-roos-coherence-data] satisfying HasSiteSections, HasSystemSections and HasRestrictionSections. There are a single RoosNormalization N and one family of Comparisons A indexed by every r : Nat. They satisfy HasProducts, HasFirstCoordinate, HasSecondCoordinate and HasDerivedModel for the original strict Roos cone and coefficientSequenceLimit. For every m : Nat, including zero, ProductCoherence, ConeCoherence and DerivedComparisonCoherence hold for these same choices N,A,P. Thus on products, on both signed coordinates and on all derived system objects the comparison for m+1 equals the composite comparison for m and 1 followed by the respective compositor. No constructibility, boundedness or normalization assumption is imposed on input systems.

proof.text: Evaluate the b/d/t square on every original system level, site object and section. Each composite is the identity under the three given section laws. Module-sheaf and tower extensionality prove the square. Exact scalar restriction is [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The inverse images F_r are exact and preserve products by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]; countable products are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact].

Choose the ordinary-limit/termwise-limit comparison fixed by all projections. Its inverse followed by the right-derived unit gives the specified unit, with K-injective equation rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_eq. [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] provides theta taking this unit to roosι on every complex. For each r form the canonical product comparison followed by the product of b_r. Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] and the strict cone map associated to b_r to obtain kappa_r and a_r. Their projection, diagonal and representative equations are HasProducts, HasFirstCoordinate, HasSecondCoordinate and HasDerivedModel.

For each triple (m,1,m+1), apply [lem-trf-roos-cone-compositor-descent] using the b/d/t square. Its product comparisons coincide with those just chosen by all projections; its cone maps coincide by both signed coordinates. Its theta equals the fixed theta because the unit is invertible on K-injective towers, and naturality along K-injective resolutions extends equality to all complexes. The representative formula and fully faithful localization identify its a with the chosen a. Its three compositor equations therefore hold for this single family at every m. Only strict products and biproducts are tested by projections.
